div.p: Most of the todays cyber-physical systems are delay tolerant. These systems can tolerate transient overloads which occur when the computation demand is greater than the available resource supply during a time interval, but recovers from the overload after a finite amount of time. In this paper, we propose a delay bound function, which is derived to check schedulability of workloads of different critical components. We characterize the criticality of a component by defining requirements on safety or performance. A safety requirement enforces a maximum delay that a high-criticality component can tolerate, while a performance requirement specifies the cumulative delay during a time interval for a low-criticality component. Using functions to specify delay requirements facilitates timing analysis for components of different levels of criticality in a cyber-physical system.

div.head: CCS CONCEPTS
div.p: • Computer systems organization → Embedded systems.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: Feedback control systems, common in many cyber-physical systems, can tolerate small delays in the feedback loop but rely on existing dbf and sbf -based techniques to determine the schedulability. Therefore, in this paper, we define delay bound function (Δbf), which can represent delays that a component may experience during a time interval for a given resource supply and demand. To the best of our knowledge, a function to validate delay specifications of components has not yet been investigated in the cyber-physical systems domain. However, the cumulative delay of a user interface to access the control plant should remain bounded for better quality of service. This is because the time required to complete tasks execution of a component is low when the cumulative delay is less, which also alternatively indicates the higher possible throughput.

The novelty of the work lies in a new way of defining acceptable delays of a cyber-physical system consisting of components that either require safety or performance. For a given resource supply and demand (sbf and dbf ), the delay of a cyber-physical system is characterized using the delay bound function based on either the max or the sum metric. The max metric is used to define the maximum delay that a component can suffer, while the sum metric defines the cumulative delay during time intervals. On the other hand, a high-criticality component has a maximum delay requirement for safety which we represent using an absolute delay bound during a time interval. Moreover, a low-criticality component has a cumulative delay specification during a time interval for a QoS represented using a periodic delay supply bound function. To analyze schedulability of a component, the absolute delay bound is compared to the delay bound function for the max metric, or the periodic delay supply bound function is compared to the delay bound function for the sum metric.

div.head: PROBLEM STATEMENT
div.p: Components in a system can tolerate delays which can be characterized as either a safety or a QoS requirement. Supply and demand bound functions (sbf and dbf ) including tolerating delays are discussed in different work [1][2][3], but deriving a delay bound function in terms of maximum delay or QoS requirement for cyber-physical systems is absent. We assume that a QoS requirement refers to the cumulative delay that a component may suffer during any possible time intervals until the hyperperiod. A safety requirement determines the maximum tolerable duration of all transient overloads in a hyperperiod. In contrast, a QoS requirement specifies the cumulative delay of all possible occurrences of transient overloads in a hyperperiod. This work therefore studies the following:
"Given a cyber-physical system, find a delay bound function to represent delay requirements of high and low criticality components. "

div.head: DELAY BOUND FUNCTION
div.p: We characterize the overloads using delays or the time difference between an overload and the associated recovery point. Using this observation, in this paper, we introduce a separate function (i.e., delay bound function) that captures delays in a component that it can suffer for a given workload and resource supply.

div.head: CONCLUSION
div.p: This paper presents how to specify delays and analyze timing to guarantee that sufficient resource supply is available to meet the demand. This analysis is applicable to systems composed of different criticality components characterized by delay specifications. Components have either a maximum or cumulative tolerable delay requirement during time intervals to specify the criticality. Such specifications are compared against the delay bound function of a component to guarantee that sufficient resources are available to meet timing requirements. A compositional framework can also take advantage of using the delay bound function when composing multiple timing requirements and the tolerable delay metrics.
